ai.definition: Mixture of Experts (MoE) architectures are a type of deep learning model design that allows for efficient inference by dynamically activating only a subset of parameters per input token.
ai.howItWorks: In MoE models, the gating network determines which of many expert sub-models to activate based on the input token. This selective activation reduces computational load and improves efficiency without sacrificing overall performance.
ai.problemSolved: MoE architectures address the challenge of maintaining high model capacity while reducing inference costs in large neural networks.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves designing the gating mechanism, training the experts, and integrating them into a larger network architecture. This process requires advanced knowledge of deep learning frameworks and efficient hardware acceleration techniques.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes defining the expert sub-models, training these models separately, developing a gating function that decides which experts to activate for each input token, and then combining all components into an integrated MoE model.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the complexity of designing effective gating mechanisms, the computational resources required for training individual experts, and the efficiency gains achieved through selective activation.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook suggests continued growth as more applications require efficient large-scale models without compromising performance.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory environment does not specifically address MoE architectures, but compliance with general data protection and privacy regulations is essential for their deployment.
ai.risks: Risks include potential instability in the gating mechanism, difficulty in training experts to perform well across diverse inputs, and challenges in optimizing performance on different hardware platforms.
ai.profitability: Profitability depends on the specific application domain. In areas where inference efficiency is critical (e.g., real-time language processing), MoE architectures can significantly reduce costs while maintaining high performance.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may focus on improving gating mechanisms, optimizing expert sub-models for different tasks, and integrating MoE into more complex model architectures.

glossary.def: A neural architecture that uses a gating mechanism to selectively activate different sub-models based on input data, enhancing inference efficiency.
The component in MoE architectures responsible for deciding which expert sub-models should be activated for each input token.

subsystems.name: Router (gating network)
subsystems.role: scores each input token and selects which experts should process it.

subsystems.name: Expert networks
subsystems.role: independent feed-forward sub-networks that specialize on different patterns in the data.

subsystems.name: Sparsity and capacity control
subsystems.role: limits how many experts each token uses and how many tokens each expert handles.

subsystems.name: Distributed training infrastructure
subsystems.role: trains many experts across multiple devices using all-to-all communication.

subsystems.name: Inference engine
subsystems.role: routes tokens efficiently at runtime and manages expert memory and batching.

buildSteps.title: Start from a dense transformer block
buildSteps.detail: Begin with a standard transformer layer where the feed-forward network is a single large module.

buildSteps.title: Replace the feed-forward network with an MoE layer
buildSteps.detail: Create many parallel expert networks instead of one, each with its own weights.

buildSteps.title: Add a router
buildSteps.detail: Insert a small linear layer that computes a score for every expert given each token's representation.

buildSteps.title: Implement top-k gating
buildSteps.detail: For each token, select the k highest-scoring experts, run the token through them, and combine outputs weighted by router probabilities.

buildSteps.title: Add auxiliary losses for load balancing
buildSteps.detail: Penalize uneven expert usage so the router spreads tokens across experts during training.

buildSteps.title: Train with expert parallelism
buildSteps.detail: Distribute experts across devices; all-to-all communication sends tokens to the selected experts and returns their outputs.

buildSteps.title: Tune capacity and routing
buildSteps.detail: Adjust the capacity factor and k to balance model quality against computational efficiency.

buildSteps.title: Optimize for inference
buildSteps.detail: Build efficient kernels that route tokens at runtime, cache expert weights, and batch variable numbers of tokens per expert.

prerequisites.why: MoE layers typically replace the feed-forward sublayers inside transformer blocks.
frameworks that support expert parallelism and all-to-all communication are essential to train large MoE models.
routing tokens to different devices creates heavy communication that must not become the bottleneck.
without them, a few experts receive most tokens while others are undertrained; research continues to improve stability.
runtime routing creates irregular workloads that general-purpose kernels handle poorly.

pathway.milestone: MoE layers used in some production language models to cut compute per token
pathway.unlocks: larger models that remain affordable to run at scale.

pathway.milestone: better routing and load balancing, enabling more experts and higher sparsity
pathway.unlocks: further gains in efficiency without degrading quality.

pathway.milestone: MoE applied to multimodal models and on-device inference
pathway.unlocks: only the relevant parts of a model run per input, saving memory and energy.

pathway.milestone: conditional computation becomes standard across AI systems
pathway.unlocks: very large models that stay cheap enough for everyday use.
